interpretationFindings: The scheduled case restrains initial-contact-driven opening; its final center gaps remain above both the initial gap and the final center target. It is not demonstrated seam closure.
Center activation rises over0–4ms, targets tighten over4–12ms, center target and activation are held over12–16ms, center releases over16–24ms, and the outer activation releases over24–32ms.

In the scheduled case, the outer cell is strictly geometrically slack throughout every accepted affine path under both endpoint target models. Its nonzero activation does not demonstrate a second loaded cable, and its activation/target changes contribute no cable work. The disabled case eventually exceeds the outer threshold but its activation remains exactly zero.

Both declared activations reach zero only at the final32ms endpoint. There is no accepted interval after complete declared deactivation. Cable energy is already zero at states12–16 because the center is disabled and the outer cell is slack.

All saved states move and both runs finish with nonzero speed. There is no unchanged-position acceptance plateau in this experiment; finite stationarity tolerance still limits what these tails establish.

Positive target work tightens the tensile threshold; activation increase stores potential and release removes potential at the new target. Negative total parameter work is not physical heat or calibrated dissipation.
interpretationLimits: Own reductions use saved binary64 q/v, exact Fraction interpolation/energy sums and exact squared-gap slack tests. Square-root gap values use90-digit Decimal approximations. This is not an independent force/work integration or contact/triangle-path audit; those belong to the separate numerical reviewer.

Per-step work/error and stationarity values are recorded solver diagnostics. Their reductions and arithmetic identities are checked here, not their constitutive evaluations. Overall work reductions retain exact rational radii; compact phase radii are ordinary float summaries, not new outward certificates.
Controls are sampled at original interval endpoints and frozen within each backward-Euler solve. Declared ramp timings do not certify continuous-time actuator forces or work.
No material damping or friction is installed. Short-run energy loss or reduced speed does not prove physical settling, calibrated attenuation, temporal/spatial convergence or a valid textile joint.

Eight free vertices, four triangles and no historical point sewing rows are a generic synthetic fixture. Actual garment correspondence, layer/side constraints, fold/turn/wrap/apex, full spatial-temporal seams and capture authorization remain separate gates.
